Spaarne Gasthuis (Haarlem)
Radiology Dept
Date: 20 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (9.3 ng/mL), prior biopsy Gleason 4+3.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume measures 18.03 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal hypo-intense lesion in the right peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows marked restricted diffusion within this region, with corresponding early enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. The lesion measures approximately 12 mm in maximum diameter. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is visualized.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone.
PSA density: 0.516 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.85247576.

PSA was noted to be rising significantly, prompting referral back to urology for re-evaluation of treatment options. Discussed the rapid PSA increase with the patient and his daughter, who manages communication.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: 25 Jul 2023 - Dr. P. van Dijk (GP): Initial presentation with elevated PSA. Transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed. Results returned showing Gleason 4+3 adenocarcinoma. Discussed findings with patient and referred to urology for initial management discussion.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1:
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. The growth pattern is characterized by cribriform and glomeruloid architecture, partly also acinar. A cribriform pattern is present. The tumour is located in the right side of the prostate.

Summary: The histological findings across the available biopsy timepoint demonstrate ISUP grade group 3 disease with high-risk architectural features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
